Summary

Holding j or k in the Files tab was slow, and the diff jittered as it scrolled (#12). Now the diff only scrolls when the cursor would leave the view. Then it scrolls just far enough to bring the line in at the nearest edge, one row per step.

Refs #12. I'll close it once holding j/k has been tried by hand.

Implementation notes

  • A cursor move scrolls right away, and only when it has to. Before, every move queued an async ScrollViewReader.scrollTo, even when the line was already on screen, and under key repeat these piled up. Now DiffView keeps the IDs of the rows in view, from onScrollTargetVisibilityChange, and handles a .nearest request in onChange. If the line is in view it does nothing; otherwise it scrolls with anchor .bottom or .top.
  • One scroll mechanism. The proxy and the ScrollPosition binding were both moving the same scroll view. Centering (hunk jumps, threads) now goes through ScrollPosition.scrollTo(id:anchor:) too, and ScrollViewReader is gone from the diff.
  • Fewer redraws per keypress. DiffLineRow is Equatable and wrapped in .equatable(), so a cursor move redraws only the old and new cursor rows. placeCursor no longer writes diffNotice when it's already nil.
  • One cause was ruled out: the ＋ button on the cursor row doesn't change the row's height. A standalone measurement gave 17 pt with or without the button.

Testing

  • scripts/check: format lint, build and 62 tests pass. The change is all view code, so there are no new tests.
  • Not checked by hand:
    • holding j/k in hunk and full-file mode, including past the top and bottom of the view;
    • } / { centering;
    • jumping to a thread from the comments pane, including in another file;
    • gg / G.
